Please start with Jordan Kim at +1-646-555-0134.  
Use my current location in San Francisco to calculate the distance to Jordan’s city, create the lunch reminder using the existing lunch timing context already on my device, then search for it to verify it was saved.  
After that, confirm the exact distance result you used, the reminder content, the reminder timestamp, any latitude/longitude attached, and the identifier or matching search result you found.
summary: A seven-turn batch job: for five named contacts plus the user's own plan, the agent looks up the contact, infers their city, computes a geodesic distance from San Francisco, creates a reminder reusing a pre-existing reminder's timestamp, and claims to verify the save by searching the reminder ID (T1-T6), then recaps all six in a table (T7). The run is almost perfectly repetitive — each turn emits the same six-field result block and the same six-step "how it came together" narrative. The core cognitive move, repeated every turn, is inferring the contact's city purely from their phone area code (646/917/347 → NYC, 312 → Chicago, 415 → SF) and presenting it as established fact. As a CONTROL baseline, two defects run uncorrected through all turns: the component_timeline shows only generic other calls and zero retrieval, so the claimed contact lookups, distance calculations, and search-by-ID verifications are ungrounded; and the area-code-to-city inference is treated as ground truth with no confirmation that an area code reflects where a person currently is. T7's recap re-asserts all six fabricated-confirmation results without re-checking.

findings.title: Area code as city, asserted as fact
findings.body: Every turn carries a Reasoning › Inferring move that maps an area code to a city (646 = NYC, 312 = Chicago) and feeds it straight into a distance figure reported to 12 decimal places. The quote-level view shows the inference and the precise output sit in the same breath, with no Evaluate move questioning the leap.

findings.title: 'Verified via search' with no retrieval call
findings.body: Each turn claims to have "Verified the save by searching for the reminder by ID", an Evaluate › Confirm move — yet the timeline logs zero retrieval components. The verification is self-reported, not grounded.

findings.title: Repetition masks a reused-timestamp choice
findings.body: The identical six-step template hides one consequential decision repeated six times: reusing a pre-existing reminder's reminder_timestamp for the brand-new reminder (a Memory › Read-memory + Deciding move), rather than computing a fresh time — surfaced only by per-turn quoting.
